In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new biomarker for the metabolic adaptations to nutritional stresses, and the underlying mechanisms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Δ15N and 12C/13C isotope effects in proteins and AA, in the context of the present study, are biomarkers for a decreased CHO oxidation and increased AA oxidation, induced by CR.
CR is associated with a decrease in CHO oxidation, and an increase in AA oxidation, which is reflected in the natural isotope abundances of tissue proteins and their constituent amino acids.

the Δ13C and Δ15N values in the tissues of obese rats subjected to CR are consistent with a decrease of CHO oxidation and an increased AA oxidation, as a result of a metabolic adaptation to the nutritional stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in obese rats subjected to CR, the Δ15N and the Δ13C levels of tissue proteins and their AA reflect a metabolic reorganization that results in an increased AA curation for energy production, at the expense of the CHO oxidation.

CR-induced metabolic adaptations are reflected by a decreased CHO oxidation, an increased AA oxidation, and a reduced AA synthesis, which are all reflected by Δ13C and Δ15N changes in tissue proteins and AA.
the CR-induced changes in Δ13C and Δ15N in tissue proteins and constitutive amino acids reflect an increased protein and non-indispensable amino acid catabolism and a decreased CHO oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tissue Δ15N and, in particular, Δ13C, in tissue proteins and AA are sensitive biomarkers of metabolic changes occurring in response to CR.
the natural isotopic composition of AA and proteins is a powerful tool to assess metabolic adaptations in response to nutritional stress.
the tissue-to-diet discrimination of 15N and of 13C in proteins and AA, as a biomarker of metabolic adaptation to a nutritional stress, reflects a decreased CHO and an increased AA oxidation.
